authorReviewNote: André Rieu founded the Johann Strauss Orchestra, as described in the inspected biography. Kennedy, Bell and Perlman are violinists but did not found this orchestra. The waltz-playing qualifier identifies Rieu's ensemble rather than a similarly named historical group. Accents and orchestra name checked.

Vanessa-Mae competed in alpine skiing at the 2014 Winter Olympics, not skating, snowboarding or bobsleigh. Actual biography and Olympic Council of Asia newsletter passage naming Vanessa Vanakorn/Vanessa-Mae, Thailand, Sochi and alpine skiing inspected. Question asks participation only, without relying on later disputed qualification findings or results. The musician and athlete are the same person.

Violin is Kennedy's especially associated string instrument. Actual biography identifies him as a violinist; cello, double bass and harp do not fit. He also plays viola and piano, so neither was offered as a false answer. Association wording avoids asserting that he plays only one instrument.

Katherine Jenkins is a mezzo-soprano, explicitly identified in the inspected biography. Soprano, contralto and tenor are distinct voice classifications, not three equally valid descriptions of her documented voice type. Hyphenation and her surname checked; no disputed classical-status claim needed.

Ballet was Bussell's established dance career before her Strictly judging. The inspected biography describes her Royal Ballet career. Flamenco, tap and Irish stepdance are distinct forms and do not match her principal career. Historical sequence avoids implying that she is still a judge.

Acosta is principally associated with ballet, supported by the inspected dancer biography. Tap, flamenco and Irish stepdance are not his principal recognised form. Most closely associated wording allows his wider choreography and performance work without turning secondary interests into multiple correct answers.

American Ballet Theatre appointed Copeland its first Black female principal in 2015. Actual official biography and dated promotion announcement corroborate the secondary biography. New York City Ballet, San Francisco Ballet and Boston Ballet are separate companies. Final stem explicitly says US ballet company, not the first Black principal across every company; year is stable and no disputed month is asked.

Michael Flatley created Lord of the Dance, supported by the inspected biography. Acosta, Bussell and Bourne are other prominent dancers/choreographers but did not create that show. No implication that Flatley created Riverdance; the distinction matters for the following Butler question.

Riverdance featured Jean Butler as its original principal female performer, as described in her inspected career biography. Lord of the Dance, Feet of Flames and Celtic Tiger are other productions, not that original role. Original qualifier fixes the production period and avoids asking about every subsequent appearance.

Piano is Holland's best-known instrument, directly supported by the inspected musician biography. Flute, trombone and viola do not match his established performing role. Best-known wording does not require proving that he has never played another instrument.

Rodgers and Bernard Edwards co-founded Chic. The actual biography identifies that partnership and band. Earth, Wind & Fire, Kool & the Gang and the Commodores are other groups with different founders. Ampersands and co-found grammar checked; guest production work would not imply co-founding those groups.

Westwood helped bring punk into mainstream fashion. Actual lead inspected; mod, hippie and preppy do not fit this documented association. New wave is also mentioned by the source and therefore was deliberately not used as a wrong option. This is distinct from the existing question about her earlier teaching profession.

Adidas began the McCartney collaboration in 2004, supported by the inspected career passage. Nike, Puma and Reebok do not match the named partnership. Began/year wording asks a historical event rather than whether a contract remains current; no claim that she has never worked with another sports company.

Tailoring was part of McQueen's training before fashion college; actual apprenticeship passages inspected. Pottery, bookbinding and glassblowing are different crafts and do not describe that training. This asks a different fact from the existing Givenchy appointment question. No changing corporate ownership detail used.

Donatella Versace became creative director after Gianni's death in 1997. Actual biography inspected; Wang, Philo and McCartney do not match that succession. Historical wording avoids incorrectly describing the company's current creative leadership. Name, possessive and year checked.

Wedding gowns are Vera Wang's particularly famous clothing category. Actual biography supports her bridal reputation. School uniforms, motorcycle leathers and military uniforms are not competing established answers. Figure-skating costumes were deliberately excluded as wrong options because she has designed them too.

Red is the signature sole colour of Christian Louboutin shoes. Actual biography describes the red sole association. Blue, green and gold do not match the signature. Signature wording does not assert that every item ever sold has a red sole; surname and British colour spelling checked.

Shoes originally made Jimmy Choo's name as a designer. The inspected biography describes his shoemaking career. Hats, scarves and watches do not match that origin. Handbags were not used as a false option because the broader brand sells them; designer-origin wording distinguishes a person's craft from the brand's later range.

Shoes are Manolo Blahnik's particularly recognised design field. Actual biography inspected; hats, watches and scarves are not competing principal answers. Wording does not deny that an established fashion business could later sell other products. Correct spelling and ordinary plural nouns checked.

The wrap dress is von Fürstenberg's signature association. Actual biography inspected. Ball gown, shift dress and halter dress do not match the specifically recognised style. Particularly known for avoids falsely claiming that she invented all wrap dresses. Umlaut and lowercase von retained correctly.

Phoebe Philo was Céline's creative director from 2008 to 2017. Actual biography inspected. Wang, McCartney and Versace did not occupy that role during the stated interval. Historical brand accent and dates checked; no implication that she remains there or that her later label is Céline.

Food and wine was Porowski's original Netflix Queer Eye specialty. Actual biography inspected. Interior design, fashion and grooming were other team members' areas. Original Netflix scope distinguishes this team from the earlier series and later personnel; no professional chef qualification asserted.

Fashion was Tan France's specialty in the original Netflix lineup. Actual biography inspected; food and wine, grooming and interior design belonged to other members. Exact name search false matches to Metropolitan France were disregarded. Same lineup scope as neighbouring questions; standalone question remains clear.

Grooming was Jonathan Van Ness's original Netflix specialty, supported by the inspected biography. Food and wine, interior design and fashion are other lineup areas. Van Ness's possessive is grammatically valid. Historical team role, not a claim that grooming exhausts their career.

Interior design was Bobby Berk's Queer Eye specialty. Actual biography describes his role and departure after the early seasons. Food and wine, grooming and fashion were other members' roles. Past-tense was avoids presenting him as an indefinitely current cast member.

Culture was Karamo Brown's specialty in the original Netflix lineup. Actual biography inspected. Food and wine, grooming and interior design are the other offered team roles. Official role label makes this specific; it is not a vague claim that one member alone has a culture.

How to Look Good Naked helped establish Gok Wan's television profile in 2006. Actual biography inspected. What Not to Wear, Ten Years Younger and Style Challenge are other makeover shows. A show question avoids falsely offering chef or DJ as wrong professions, since he has worked in those areas too.

Susannah Constantine formed the original BBC What Not to Wear duo with Trinny Woodall. Actual biography inspected. Mary Portas, Kelly Hoppen and Gok Wan are other television/style personalities, not that duo partner. Original BBC scope distinguishes adaptations and later unrelated programmes.

Interior design is Hoppen's principal design field, supported by the inspected biography. Fashion, jewellery and automotive design do not match her principal recognition. Particularly associated wording does not make an absolute assertion about every commercial collaboration.

Hairdresser is Nicky Clarke's best-known profession. Actual biography identifies the celebrity hairdresser. Makeup artist, interior designer and jeweller do not match that established role. Distinguishes the person from the hair-products brand; no current salon ownership claim.

Charlotte Tilbury built her career as a makeup artist before launching her cosmetics brand. Actual training and assistant/career passages inspected. Perfumer, nail technician and hair colourist do not describe that founding career. Past-career wording avoids confusing her later brand's perfume and beauty product range with her earlier profession.

Mentalism and illusion describe Derren Brown's recognised performance work. Actual biography inspected. Opera, ballet and circus acrobatics do not match that work. Painting was excluded as a false choice because he also paints. Wording makes no claim that supernatural powers are real.

David Blaine's Street Magic television special appeared in 1997. Actual biography inspected. Brown, Angel and Copperfield are different performers, not the star of that special. Specific title/year anchors a historical event rather than a vague question about who performs street magic.

Penn Jillette is Teller's speaking partner in the double act, supported by the inspected Penn biography. Blaine, Brown and Copperfield are other magicians. Speaking-partner wording describes the act, not an assertion that Teller never speaks in private or on any occasion.

Las Vegas is the Rio residency's city, supported by the same inspected Penn career biography. Los Angeles, New York and San Francisco do not match that venue. Long-running residency wording asks its location, not a current nightly schedule. Distinct fact from naming the speaking partner; reverse Teller identity draft was rejected as redundant.

Criss Angel starred in Mindfreak, supported by the inspected biography. Blaine, Brown and Jillette are other performers. Short show title avoids giving Angel's name away in the stem while remaining identifiable. Spelling Criss, not Chris, checked.

David Copperfield made the Statue of Liberty appear to disappear in the 1983 television illusion. Actual biography inspected. Blaine, Brown and Angel do not match that performance. Appear to disappear avoids saying that the statue literally vanished; illusionist distinguishes the performer from Dickens's fictional character. Other existing Copperfield questions concern different events.

Physics is Professor Brian Cox's academic discipline, supported by the inspected scientist biography. Chemistry, archaeology and computer science do not match. Professor distinguishes him from the actor. Music and astronomy were deliberately excluded as wrong choices because his musician history and astrophysical work could make them defensible.

The Sky at Night is the BBC astronomy programme Aderin-Pocock joined as co-presenter in 2014. Actual biography inspected. Countryfile, Antiques Roadshow and University Challenge do not match the stated astronomy role. Public professional name and historical date checked; no current legal-name claim or unchanged-future-hosting assumption.

Chris Packham regularly presented both The Really Wild Show and Springwatch, supported by the inspected career biography. Titchmarsh, Don and Dimmock are chiefly gardening presenters and do not match that pair. Michaela Strachan was excluded as a wrong answer because she also presented both. Both-series qualifier and regular role make the offered answer unique.
